components.gap: The Remarks qualifying Theorem 3.4.17 (Durrett p. 157) are not all supplied. Present: validity for all n and x with nontrivial content only for n >= 10 (annex 318-323) and the impossibility of a uniformly faster rate for fair signs (annex 438-448). source_locators.content: Remark: x^{-alpha} tails give S_n/n^{1/alpha} => a non-chi limit

components.gap: The excluded-power-tail item (lines 220-228; annex 721-732) proves only that tails P(|X| > x) = x^{-alpha}, 0 < alpha < 2, admit no normal limit. The source's Remark (Durrett p. 152) also claims that for these laws S_n/n^{1/alpha} converges weakly to a limit which is not chi (deferred to Section 3.6). That positive claim, with its n^{1/alpha} normalization, is not stated on the route, even as a cited forward result.

Levy (footnote to Theorem 1, p. 172); (ii) the section's framing claims on p. 172: the domain of attraction of a law and of a type, with laws of the same type having the same domain; that by Section 33 the stable laws, and only these, have nonempty domains of attraction; that determining these domains is a fundamental problem of stable-law theory solved completely in Section 35; and that the normal law attracts a very wide class of laws whereas the other stable laws attract only laws whose character recalls the attracting law.
